hero.title: Link Charts vs Bitly
hero.subtitle: Bitly's free plan changed in 2025. See what each URL shortener gives you today without paying.
hero.verdict: Bitly is the better-known name, but since February 2025 its free plan shows ads before the redirect and creates at most 5 links per month. Link Charts keeps redirects ad-free, creation unlimited, and full analytics free — including a score that separates human clicks from bots.

changes.intro: Free-plan users felt three concrete changes — and they explain why so many people started looking for an alternative:

items.title: Ads on free links
items.desc: Free-plan links now show an ad page (interstitial) before the destination — including old links created before the change.

items.title: 5 links per month
items.desc: The free plan now creates up to 5 links, 2 QR codes, and 3 custom back-halves per month, and analytics is limited to click counts.

items.title: Basic features moved to paid plans
items.desc: Detailed analytics requires the Core plan (US$ 8/month billed annually, 100 links/month, 30–90 days of retention). Custom domains only start at Growth (~US$ 29/month).

changes.note: Source: Bitly's public pricing pages and official blog, checked in July 2026.

table.disclaimer: Bitly data refers to the free plan and public pricing as of July 2026; subject to change.

choose.linkChartsBody: You want detailed analytics for free with no monthly cap, you won't accept an ad between the click and the destination, and you care about traffic quality (knowing whether clicks are real) and a custom subdomain without paying.
choose.rivalBody: You already pay for a Core or Growth plan, rely on the Bitly ecosystem's integrations, and need the most globally recognized brand.

items.q: Link Charts or Bitly: which free plan pays off more?
items.a: On the free plan, Link Charts delivers more analytics: geography by city, device, browser, traffic source, and a quality score that flags bot traffic — all in real time, with ad-free redirects. Bitly's free plan creates 5 links per month and shows click counts only, but it wins on brand recognition and integrations.

items.q: Is Bitly really free?
items.a: Bitly has a free plan, but today it creates up to 5 links and 2 QR codes per month, shows only click counts, and since February 2025 it displays ads before the redirect — including on old links. Detailed analytics starts on the Core plan (US$ 8/month billed annually).

items.q: Does Bitly put ads on my links?
items.a: On the free plan, yes. Since February 2025, free Bitly links can show an ad page (interstitial) before reaching the destination, and the change also applied to links created before that date. Link Charts redirects never show ads.

items.q: How do I see which city a link's clicks came from?
items.a: In Link Charts, every short link shows click geography (country and city), plus device and browser, in the real-time analytics panel.

items.q: How do I know if my link's clicks are real or from bots?
items.a: Link Charts calculates a traffic quality score (0–100) that classifies each click as organic, suspicious, or likely fraud — a feature most URL shorteners don't offer.

items.q: Can I use my own subdomain with the URL shortener?
items.a: Yes. Link Charts supports up to 3 custom subdomains, including on free usage, while at Bitly custom domains only start on the Growth plan (~US$ 29/month).

hero.title: How to tell if your link's clicks are real or bots
hero.subtitle: Not every click is a person. Learn how to spot automated traffic — and how Link Charts does it for you.
hero.verdict: Bots inflate your numbers and hide who actually cares. Link Charts scores every click from 0 to 100 and separates organic traffic from suspicious traffic automatically.

score.intro: Every click starts at 100 points and loses points for each sign of automation. The result falls into one of three tiers:

tiers.label: Organic
tiers.desc: Behavior consistent with a real person.

tiers.label: Suspicious
tiers.desc: Some signs of automation — worth a look.

tiers.label: Likely fraud
tiers.desc: Multiple signs of a bot or automated click.

score.scoreExplain: Known bots (crawlers, spiders, scrapers) get a 0 outright and land in likely fraud.

signals.sectionTitle: The signals that give a bot away
signals.intro: A human click leaves a coherent trail. These are the signals that most often expose automation:

items.title: Datacenter IP
items.desc: Clicks coming from servers and cloud — not residential or mobile networks — are a strong sign of automation.

items.title: Missing browser headers
items.desc: Real browsers report language and platform. Bots often arrive without that information.

items.title: Clicks too fast
items.desc: Several clicks on the same link within seconds point to a script, not a person.

items.title: Device contradictions
items.desc: When what the browser claims doesn't add up — for example, it says mobile, but the signals point to desktop.

items.title: High-frequency sessions
items.desc: Dozens of clicks in the same session fall outside a normal visitor's pattern.

items.title: Programmatic access
items.desc: Arrivals via API or automation instead of a real click from an app or browser.

auto.sectionTitle: How Link Charts does this for you
auto.body: You don't have to investigate anything by hand. For every click, Link Charts evaluates these signals in real time, computes the quality score, and labels the click as organic, suspicious, or likely fraud. In the dashboard, you filter out suspicious traffic in one click and see your real numbers — for free.

items.q: How do I know if my link's clicks are real or from bots?
items.a: Link Charts scores every click from 0 to 100 based on signals like datacenter IPs, missing browser headers, clicks that are too fast, and device contradictions, and labels each one as organic, suspicious, or likely fraud — automatically.

items.q: What is bot traffic on shortened links?
items.a: It's any click that doesn't come from a person: crawlers, scrapers, automatic previews, and scripts. It inflates the click count without representing real interest.

items.q: Why does my link have many clicks but little conversion?
items.a: It's often bot or low-quality traffic inflating the count. Separating organic from suspicious reveals the number that actually matters.

items.q: Does Link Charts detect fake clicks automatically?
items.a: Yes. Detection happens in real time on every click, with no setup, and the result shows up in the free dashboard as a quality score and tier (organic, suspicious, or likely fraud).

items.q: What does a click's quality score mean?
items.a: It's a 0-to-100 rating that sums up how likely the click came from a real person. The more signs of automation, the lower the score.

steps.title: Share and track
steps.desc: Use the link on Instagram, flyers and ads. Every tap becomes data: time, city and device, in real time.

why.sectionTitle: Why not share the raw wa.me link
why.body: WhatsApp's default link works, but it hides everything: you never know how many people tapped it, where they came from or which promotion brought each contact. It also exposes your phone number in the address itself and carries no brand. The short link fixes all three: it hides the number, carries your name and turns every click into a statistic — so you learn whether your audience comes from Instagram, flyers or ads.

metrics.sectionTitle: What you see in every click
metrics.intro: WhatsApp doesn't count how many people reached you. The short link does:

items.title: How many people clicked
items.desc: The real tap count on your link, day by day — the thermometer of every promotion.

items.title: Peak hours
items.desc: Find out when your audience clicks most, so you post and advertise at the right time.

items.title: City and region
items.desc: See where interested people come from — essential for local business, delivery and events.

items.title: Real clicks vs. bots
items.desc: Link Charts separates human clicks from bots and scanners, so the number you watch is the one that matters.

auto.sectionTitle: Link Charts does this for free
auto.body: Paste your WhatsApp link, customize the ending and you're done — no account needed to start. With the free account you keep every link in one dashboard, with real-time analytics, a print-ready QR code and even a branded subdomain.

items.q: Can I create a short link for a WhatsApp group?
items.a: Yes. Paste the group invite link (chat.whatsapp.com) into Link Charts and share the short link. You track how many people tapped the invite — and with the free account you can edit the destination later, pointing to a new group without changing the link you shared.

items.q: Does the WhatsApp short link expire?
items.a: No. The link keeps working with no expiry date and no click limit on the free plan.

items.q: How do I know how many people joined my group through the link?
items.a: The short link counts how many people tapped the invite and opened WhatsApp. Joining happens inside the app, but the click count is the best thermometer of each promotion — with time, city and device for every tap.

items.q: Do I need to pay or sign up to shorten a WhatsApp link?
items.a: No. Shortening is free with no sign-up. The free account adds the full dashboard: history, destination editing, QR codes and analytics for all your links.

items.q: Does it work with wa.me, api.whatsapp.com and group links?
items.a: Yes, all of them: wa.me (with or without a preset message), api.whatsapp.com and chat.whatsapp.com group invites. Link Charts shortens any of them and counts clicks the same way.

hero.title: Free Bitly alternative: the best options in 2026
hero.subtitle: Since February 2025, Bitly itself warns that free-plan links may show an ad preview page before the destination — and the free plan creates at most 5 links per month. We compared the options that are left, with the source and date behind every number.
hero.verdict: If you want real analytics without paying, Link Charts is the most complete alternative: no monthly link limit, ad-free redirects and country, city, device and traffic-source reports on the free plan. To just shorten quickly with no account, TinyURL and encurtador.dev do the job — but TinyURL shows no clicks without the paid plan.

disclosure.sectionTitle: Before the list: who wrote this
disclosure.body: Link Charts is one of the shorteners compared here — and it comes first. Instead of hiding that, we state it: the criteria are published below and every claim about a competitor comes from that service's own official page, checked in August 2026. Where we could not confirm a fact, we say so on the line itself.

criteria.intro: A free shortener comes down to four questions. They apply to every service on the list:

items.title: How many links on the free plan
items.desc: The first ceiling you hit. Bitly allows 5 links per month; the other options on the list publish no monthly limit.

items.title: Ad-free redirect
items.desc: Whether the visitor sees an ad screen before reaching the destination. Every extra screen between the click and your content costs you people along the way.

items.title: Analytics included for free
items.desc: Counting clicks is the bare minimum. What separates the options is getting country, city, device and traffic source without a paid plan.

items.title: Sign-up and real cost
items.desc: Whether you can use it without an account, and which feature the service starts charging for.

options.intro: Four free options, with what each does well and where each one stops.

items.name: Link Charts
items.tagline: Brazilian shortener with full analytics on the free plan.
pros: No monthly link limit and a direct redirect, with no ad page.
Country, city, device, browser, traffic source and peak hours included for free.
Traffic-quality score that separates human clicks from bots — a feature we did not find on the free plans of the other options on this list, as checked in August 2026.
Shortens with no sign-up; the free account adds a dashboard, QR codes and up to 3 branded subdomains.
cons: New and small next to Bitly: almost no brand recognition outside Brazil.
Interface and support designed in Portuguese — if you need a globally recognized name, another option may fit better.
items.note: Disclosure: this site belongs to Link Charts. The criteria are above; check them and decide for yourself.

items.name: TinyURL
items.tagline: The shortest path to a short link with no account.
pros: Free and sign-up free, with the option to choose the link ending.
cons: Shows no clicks on the free plan — tracking sits in the Pro plan, advertised from US$ 9.99 per month on TinyURL's own blog; price trackers list a higher figure for monthly billing (checked August 2026).
No breakdown by country, city, device or source without paying.

items.name: encurtador.dev
items.tagline: Brazilian, sign-up free and with an open stats page.
pros: Free and account free, with no link limit published on the site itself.
Has a public stats page: paste the short link and see the numbers, no login.
cons: With no account there is no dashboard bringing the history of all your links together.
The infrastructure promises (99.99% uptime) come from the site itself, with no independent audit.

items.name: encurtador.com.br
items.tagline: Brazilian, with a click counter and an optional free account.
pros: Free, with a click counter, and the page itself promises as many links as you want.
Optional free account to organize the links you create.
cons: The line between free and Premium is unclear: features such as UTM, tracking pixels and API appear as paid.
We could not read the full terms — the page blocked our automated access in August 2026.

bitly.intro: Three concrete changes to the free plan explain the search for an alternative:

items.title: Ad before the destination
items.desc: By the company's own notice, free-plan links may now show an ad preview page before taking the visitor to the destination — including links created years earlier, with no action from whoever created them.

items.title: 5 links per month
items.desc: The current limit is 5 short links, 2 QR codes and 3 custom back-halves per month. Beyond that, only with a paid plan.

items.title: Click counts only
items.desc: The free plan shows total clicks and scans, with no breakdown by country, city, device or source. A custom domain starts at the Growth plan (US$ 29/month billed annually).

bitly.note: Sources: Bitly's official pricing page and blog, checked in August 2026; the company's notice about the ad preview page is from February 2025, in the wording published at the time — the support article about ads did not open for our check.

bitly.crossLinkLabel: Detailed comparison: Link Charts vs Bitly

items.q: What is the best free Bitly alternative in 2026?
items.a: It depends on what you need. For detailed analytics without paying, Link Charts is the most complete option on the list: no monthly link limit, ad-free redirects and country, city, device and traffic-source reports on the free plan. To just shorten quickly with no account, TinyURL and encurtador.dev do the job — but TinyURL shows no clicks without the paid plan.

items.q: Why did Bitly start showing ads on links?
items.a: In February 2025 Bitly warned that free-plan links may go through an ad preview page before the destination. The notice also covered old links, created years earlier, with no action from whoever created them.

items.q: How many links does Bitly's free plan allow today?
items.a: Five short links per month, plus 2 QR codes and 3 custom back-halves, according to the official pricing page checked in August 2026. Free-plan analytics are limited to click and scan counts, with no breakdown by country, city or device.

items.q: Is there a free link shortener with real analytics?
items.a: Yes. Link Charts includes country and city, device, browser, traffic source and hourly evolution on the free plan, plus a score that separates human clicks from bots. encurtador.dev also shows clicks with no sign-up, in a more basic form.

items.q: Can I migrate the links I already have on Bitly?
items.a: The bit.ly links you already shared keep pointing to Bitly — there is no ownership transfer between shorteners. The practical path is to create new links on the alternative you pick and swap the address wherever you still control the distribution: bio, ads and new material. That is why it pays to choose carefully now.
